old_caption: The video captures a serene scene of a small waterfall cascading over rocks, surrounded by autumn leaves. The water flows smoothly, creating a gentle stream that splashes against the rocks, some of which are partially covered in ice. The rocks are large and dark, with patches of green moss adding texture to their surfaces. Scattered around the base of the waterfall are vibrant red and orange leaves, indicating the season is fall. The leaves appear wet, possibly from the misty spray of the waterfall. The overall atmosphere is peaceful and natural, with no visible animals or human characters present. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on the waterfall and its immediate surroundings, allowing viewers to fully absorb the tranquil beauty of the scene.

caption: The video captures a fixed close view of a small stream cascading through a narrow gap between two large rocks. The right boulder is coated in green moss, while translucent ice formations arch over and beside the water channel on the left and below. Red and orange autumn leaves lie scattered across the wet rock surfaces and frozen edges. A thin vertical sheet of falling water pours steadily through the gap into a dark, churning pool at the bottom center. The bright white streaks of the column and the foam spilling over the upper ice edge continually shift shape and position, marking an ongoing flow. The pool beneath shows moving bubbles and ripples whose pattern changes as the water strikes it. All solid elements, including the mossy rock, ice arches and protruding leaves, hold their positions without camera movement.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
